title: Scammers demand crypto from stranded ships in Strait of Hormuz: Report
summary: Shipping companies stranded near the Strait of Hormuz are reportedly being targeted by scammers posing as Iranian authorities, demanding Bitcoin or USDt for “safe passage.”

title: Philippines SEC warns on dYdX, six other unauthorized crypto platforms
summary: Promoters of flagged platforms may face fines of up to 5 million Philippine pesos ($89,000) or up to 21 years in prison under Philippine securities law.

title: Bank of Korea governor backs CBDCs, deposit tokens in first address
summary: New Bank of Korea governor Shin Hyun-song supported CBDCs and deposit tokens in his first address, while stablecoins were notably absent from his remarks.

title: Bitcoin risks losing $70K as Strategy's STRC slips below $100
summary: STRC's dropped below its $100 par value, indicating that Strategy will likely pause Bitcoin buying this week, which could help the bears pull price down to $70,000.

title: European banks tap Fireblocks for MiCA-compliant euro stablecoin
summary: A 12-bank European consortium led by Qivalis is partnering with Fireblocks to develop a regulated euro stablecoin under MiCA, targeting launch in the second half of 2026.

title: Inside the 'fake police raid' that forced a $1M Bitcoin transfer
summary: A fake police raid enabled a $1 million Bitcoin robbery, exposing the rise of wrench attacks and the shift from digital hacks to physical crypto threats.

title: Singapore’s OCBC launches tokenized gold fund on Ethereum and Solana
summary: The value of tokenized real-world assets on public blockchains is estimated at more than $29 billion, up more than 10% in the last 30 days.

title: Arbitrum freezes $71M of Ether connected to Kelp exploit
summary: Griff Green, a member of Arbitrum’s security council, said the group acted with input from law enforcement and “did not make this decision lightly."

title: US senator urges delay of CLARITY Act Senate markup until May: Report
summary: US Senator Thom Tillis said members of the crypto and banking industries still need more time to be heard.

title: Code is ‘functional’ free speech under the First Amendment: Coin Center
summary: Crypto software developers are concerned about whether they may be held criminally liable for publishing their software, following high-profile convictions last year.
